body:
Ardian, a Paris-based global private investment firm, has raised €1 billion ( US$1.1 billion ) for a private-equity fund dedicated to the semiconductor value chain.

Focused on Europe, Ardian Semiconductor aims to enable companies to grow into global leaders in their markets. The platform comprises close to €700 million of fund commitments alongside co-investments.

According to Ardian, the successful fundraise reflects strong investor demand for a specialist strategy targeting scalable companies in growing segments of the semiconductor industry, at a time when AI adoption and the strategic importance of semiconductor supply chains are accelerating globally.

The strategy targets companies with scalable potential across the semiconductor value chain, combining detailed analysis of technology megatrends with disciplined asset selection focused on non-cyclical value creation drivers.

The fund is positioned around an active pipeline of opportunities, primarily in Europe and also in North America and Asia.

Global semiconductor sales exceeded US$1 trillion in the first eight months of 2026 alone, a level previously not expected before 2030. The market is now forecast to reach US$1.6 trillion in 2026 and US$2.5 trillion by 2030.

Growth is also broadening beyond advanced processors and memory. AI data centres require more specialty semiconductors ( power, analog, photonics ), as power delivery, interconnections and testing have become new bottlenecks, Ardian says. Physical AI, through smart vehicles, robotics and AI-enabled devices, will extend this demand further.

Ardian Semiconductor was formed through an exclusive strategic partnership with Silian Partners, a team of highly successful senior executives from the semiconductor industry with more than 150 years of combined experience in the space.

The capital raise attracted commitments from both new ( 58% ) and existing investors ( 42% ), including government agencies, sovereign wealth funds, semiconductor corporates, insurance companies and private wealth clients. MENA investors accounted for more than two-fifths ( 41% ) of the capital raise alongside strong interest from French investors ( 24% ).

The fund has already been deployed across four investments – Vsora, Centrotherm, Synergie Cad and Ion Beam Services – companies that span key links of the semiconductor value chain, from AI chip design to production and test equipment.
